applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) which show four transformer pad locations adjacent to driveways. Transformer pads are drawn as rectangular symbols within landscaped islands adjacent to paved access routes. No specifications or annotations are provided on any sheet indicating the surface material of the transformer pad access areas. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad in a landscaped/unpaved island area between a sidewalk and drive aisle. No notes or details specify that access surfaces are HMAC or PCC pavement, nor are any structural specifications or load capacity information provided.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformer pad access surfaces to be all-weather prepared surfaces (HMAC or PCC pavement). UCM § 1.3.16 and LDC § 25-12-173 establish that access surfaces must be hot mix asphaltic concrete or Portland cement concrete pavement capable of supporting required vehicle weight. The site plan shows transformer pads in landscaped areas adjacent to driveways but does not confirm the pad access surfaces themselves are prepared pavement. Gravel, grass, or unpaved surfaces do not meet this requirement. Without explicit specification and detail of the transformer pad access surface material as HMAC or PCC with adequate structural design, compliance cannot be verified. The preliminary electrical plan does not include construction details or material specifications for transformer pad surfaces.
findings.comment: Transformer pad access surfaces not specified as hot mix asphaltic concrete (HMAC) or Portland cement concrete (PCC) pavement. Provide detailed construction specifications and engineering calculations confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces meet all-weather pavement requirements and load capacity standards.

applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21 for access surface design and load capacity documentation. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows spot elevations and contour lines across the site but does NOT show transformer pad locations or elevations. Sheets 9 and 21 show four transformer pads adjacent to paved driveways but provide no pavement design calculations, structural details, or load capacity specifications. No engineering calculations or structural design documentation is visible on any sheet confirming the access surfaces can support the required 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with maximum 32,530 lbs rear axle weight.
findings.reasoning: Code requires access surfaces to be capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with 32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight without damage. This requires structural design calculations appropriate to soil conditions and pavement type. The site plan and grading plan do not show transformer pad locations with associated structural details or pavement design calculations. Without structural calculations specific to each transformer pad location, it cannot be verified that the access surfaces meet load capacity requirements. The burden is on the applicant to demonstrate compliance through engineering design.
findings.comment: Structural capacity of transformer pad access surfaces not documented. Provide pavement design calculations and structural engineering certification confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces can support 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight) without damage.

applicableAreas: Transformer pads adjacent to driveways where distances exceed 6 feet
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads are shown adjacent to paved driveways within approximately 6 feet based on visual scale (1" = 20'). However, specific measurement dimensions are not labeled on the plans. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" in a landscaped island between a sidewalk and drive aisle curb. No laydown curb specifications, dimensions, or details are shown on any sheet. No notes or details indicate whether laydown curbs are provided or what their specifications are (width, height, load capacity).
findings.reasoning: Code requires laydown curbs when transformer pads are not within 6 feet of drivable surface, with minimum 12-foot width and load capacity for transformer truck loads. The site plan shows transformers adjacent to driveways but does not explicitly measure the distances or confirm they are within 6 feet. More importantly, no laydown curb specifications are shown if any are required. Without clear dimensional verification of distances and explicit design details for any laydown curbs (including 12-foot minimum width and load capacity specifications), compliance cannot be determined. The exact location relationship of pads to curbs and drivable surfaces is ambiguous without precise measurements.
findings.comment: Distances from transformer pads to drivable surfaces not dimensionally verified on plans, and laydown curb specifications not shown. Provide dimensioned measurements confirming distances from each transformer pad to nearest drivable surface, and if distances exceed 6 feet, provide laydown curb details with minimum 12-foot width and adequate load capacity specifications.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations at Buildings 1, 2, 4, and 7
findings.observation: Examined Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Grading Plan (Sheet 11). The buildings are shown as slab-on-grade construction on the site plan. However, Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does NOT show transformer pad locations, so it is impossible to verify whether transformers are located over basement levels, subgrade parking garages, or other subsurface structures. The site plan shows buildings are slab-on-grade but building sections showing subsurface conditions are not provided in the available sheets. Site plan notes indicate parking exists (88 spaces: 10 surface + 78 garage), but the relationship between individual transformer locations and the subsurface parking structure locations cannot be verified from the available plans.
findings.reasoning: Code requires verification that transformer pads are not located over basement levels, subgrade parking garages, or other subsurface structures. The site has underground parking (78 garage spaces) but transformer pad locations are not shown on the grading plan or any section views. Without building sections or subsurface structural plans showing the locations of underground parking areas and vaults in relation to each transformer pad location, it is impossible to verify compliance. The preliminary electrical plan shows only the top-level transformer pad symbols without subsurface coordination.
findings.comment: Relationship between transformer pad locations and subsurface structures not verified. Provide building sections and parking structure plans showing the subsurface conditions below each transformer pad location, confirming no transformers are located over basement levels, subgrade parking garages, or other subsurface structures.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths from transformers to meters on all eight buildings
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) which shows electrical routing from transformers to meters. Blue lines represent underground electric lines routed from transformers through pull boxes to meters on buildings. Visual inspection of the routing paths shows multiple turns. For example, routing from the transformer pad adjacent to Building 8 to the building's meters shows approximately 2 turn angles. However, the plan is schematic and does not explicitly count or label the number of 90-degree bends at each turn location. For many routing paths, multiple 90-degree turns are visually apparent as the lines navigate around building footprints and follow driveway layouts, but exact turn counts are not documented.
findings.reasoning: Code requires maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer and meter. While the electrical routing shows various path configurations, the plan does not explicitly document or count the number of 90-degree bends in each routing path. Without precise notation of turn counts, it is unclear whether any routing exceeds the maximum of two 90-degree turns. Some routing paths appear to have more than two distinct directional changes. The schematic nature of the plan makes definitive turn counting difficult without detailed field verification or explicit turn counts on the design.
findings.comment: Number of 90-degree turns in electrical routing from each transformer to meter not documented. Provide detailed electrical routing schedule or plan annotations showing the count of 90-degree bends in the conduit path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter(s), confirming maximum two 90-degree bends.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths crossing or running near storm drain infrastructure
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) and Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan). Sheet 21 shows blue electrical routing lines (marked 'E') crossing or running near dashed lines representing storm drain (SD) lines marked with square inlet symbols. Multiple crossing locations are visible on the plan. For example, electrical routing crosses storm drain lines between Building 2 and Building 8, and near Building 4. However, no dimension labels or callouts indicate the clearance distance between the electrical lines and storm drain lines at these crossing locations. No specifications confirm that minimum 12-inch clearance (or operational practice 5-foot clearance) is maintained.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 12-inch clearance between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure. While the plans show electrical lines and drainage infrastructure, the clearance distances at crossing points are not dimensionally verified. Without specific clearance measurements at each crossing, compliance cannot be confirmed. The visual separation on a 1" = 20' scale plan may be deceptive and does not constitute adequate verification of actual clearances. Engineering coordination between electrical and drainage design should document these clearances explicitly.
findings.comment: Clearances between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure not documented. Provide dimension details or engineering notes confirming that electrical conduit routing maintains minimum 12-inch clearance from all drainage pipes, storm drains, and related infrastructure at all crossing and adjacent locations.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing from public ROW entry point through transformer and meter locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) which shows blue electrical routing lines entering from Valley View Road (public right-of-way) on the left side of the plan. The routing line is labeled "Underground Electric Line" where it enters from the public ROW. The majority of the electrical routing network shown on the site appears to be within private property boundaries, but the entry point and initial routing segment from Valley View Road into the site are clearly shown originating in public ROW. The plan does not explicitly denote property line boundaries along the entire routing path to verify that the routing is 100% on private property after connection to the system.
findings.reasoning: Code requires electrical routing from riser to transformer and meter to be 100% on private property. Sheet 21 shows the electrical routing line entering from Valley View Road (public ROW). While most of the internal site routing appears to be on private property, the plans do not clearly verify that all electrical routing from the initial connection point is on private property and does not route through any public easement areas. The entry point in the ROW raises questions about whether initial segments comply with the 100% private property requirement.
findings.comment: Electrical routing from public utility connection point to transformer and meters not verified as 100% on private property. Provide routing diagram or plan notes clearly indicating property line boundaries and confirming that all electrical routing from the initial public utility connection point through transformers to all meters is located entirely on private property and does not route through public ROW or public easements.

applicableAreas: Transformer locations near Building 2 with nearby 'Vault Easement' label
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan). Near Building 2, one of the four transformer pad locations is accompanied by a text label reading "Vault Easement" pointing to a dashed rectangular boundary area that also contains an "Electrical Pull Box" label. This label indicates the presence of a vault easement in that location. However, no vault design details are shown on this sheet or any other electrical, grading, or site plan sheet in the available documentation. There are no vault door specifications, vault interior dimensions, access details, fire rating notes, ventilation provisions, or any other vault-specific design information visible.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformer vaults to be submitted to AE Network Design for approval, and vault location, access, and elevation must be coordinated with AE Network Design (allow 3-6 months for vault design review per UCM § 1.11.1.D). The presence of a "Vault Easement" label suggests a subsurface vault may be planned, but the preliminary electrical plan provides no vault design documentation or AE Network Design coordination evidence. If a transformer vault is being planned (indicated by the easement), it should be accompanied by detailed vault design, load calculations, fire rating specifications, and documented AE Network Design approval. The lack of vault design details alongside the easement label creates ambiguity about whether a vault is actually planned or if this is merely an easement designation.
findings.comment: Transformer vault is referenced by 'Vault Easement' label on electrical plan, but no vault design specifications or evidence of AE Network Design approval is provided. If transformer vault service is proposed, provide complete vault design including interior dimensions, access specifications, fire ratings, ventilation details, load calculations, and documented AE Network Design approval. If vault is not proposed, clarify the purpose of the vault easement notation.

applicableAreas: Transformer locations and proposed service configuration
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) showing four transformer pads labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". The property is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704, which is in South Austin. According to facts.md, there is no Network Area designation at this property and no regulating plan applies. The Network Area is defined in UCM § 1.11.5 as the downtown Austin area providing vault-only service. The site location is outside downtown and the project facts confirm no Network Area status. However, Sheet 21 shows one transformer location with an adjacent "Vault Easement" label, suggesting a possible vault configuration may be planned. If transformer vaults are being proposed at this location outside the Network Area, this would violate code requirements (UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.10.4 require vault-only service in Network Area; outside Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted or in niches per UCM § 1.5.2.6).
findings.reasoning: Code limits transformer vault rooms to the downtown Network Area only (UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5). Outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted or located in niches (with AE Design consultation). The site is clearly outside the Network Area (South Lamar area, no Network Area designation per facts.md). The presence of a "Vault Easement" label on Sheet 21 near Building 2 raises the question of whether a transformer vault room (subsurface room with multiple transformers) is being proposed outside the Network Area. If the vault easement indicates a planned vault room (rather than just vault infrastructure within a padmount config), this would be a code violation. Clarification is needed about the exact nature of the vault easement and whether transformer vault rooms are being proposed.
findings.comment: Vault Easement notation appears on electrical plan for property outside downtown Network Area. Clarify whether transformer vault rooms (subsurface rooms) are proposed; if so, provide evidence that site is within the downtown Network Area per UCM § 1.11.5. If site is outside Network Area (as facts indicate), transformer vaults are prohibited; transformers must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation per UCM § 1.5.2.6.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21. Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads, and Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad location in a landscaped island. However, no dimensions or clearance zones are labeled on either sheet. The 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance is not dimensionally shown or verified on any plan. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations, so the vertical clearance above the pads cannot be verified. The site has extensive retaining walls and grade changes up to 9+ feet, creating constrained spaces. Without dimensional verification of the set-up area and vertical clearance, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.reasoning: Code requires a minimum 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area in front of transformer equipment with 35-foot vertical clearance above. The site plans do not dimensionally verify that this area is provided at each transformer location. The site's constrained layout with retaining walls and significant grade changes makes this requirement difficult to verify without explicit dimensioning. The set-up area must be maintained clear of obstructions. Without plan annotations confirming the set-up area dimensions and vertical clearance at each transformer location, compliance is unclear.
findings.comment: 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance not dimensionally verified on plans. Provide dimensioned site plan details showing the 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area in front of each transformer pad, with clearance to buildings, structures, and other obstructions, and confirm 35-foot vertical clearance above each pad is maintained.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. Neither sheet provides dimensioned set-up areas, vertical clearance measurements, or AE Design approval documentation for the transformer equipment. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad in a landscaped island adjacent to a driveway and sidewalk area. The constrained site layout with retaining walls and limited maneuvering space suggests that the standard 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance may be difficult to achieve without deviations. No AE Design approval documentation is visible on the plans authorizing any reduced clearances or alternative configurations.
findings.reasoning: Code allows for AE Design-approved deviations from standard set-up area and clearance requirements. However, any such deviations require documented AE Design approval with specific conditions. The preliminary plans show no evidence of such approval. Without either confirmation of standard set-up areas and clearances, or documented AE Design approval of deviations, compliance cannot be verified. The site's constrained layout strongly suggests that deviations from standard requirements may be necessary, but these must be explicitly approved and documented.
findings.comment: Adequate set-up area and clearances at transformer equipment not documented, and AE Design approval of any deviations not shown. Provide either (1) dimensioned plans confirming 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance at all transformers, or (2) documented AE Design written approval of specific project deviations with approval conditions clearly noted on plans.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations and corresponding meter locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. Meters are shown on the exterior of all eight buildings. The four transformer pads are located in various positions around the site (near Buildings 1, 2, 4, and 7). While the 2D schematic plan shows the general proximity of transformers and meters, it is impossible from a top-down plan view to determine unobstructed visual line of sight. The site has buildings, landscaping, retaining walls, sidewalks, and other vertical obstructions that could block the line of sight between some transformers and their serving meters. For example, the transformer south of Building 4 to the meters on Building 4 might be blocked by the building itself depending on building geometry and roof configuration.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformers to be in direct line of sight to meters. This requires not only proximity but also unobstructed visual path from the transformer to the meter location. A 2D plan cannot adequately verify line of sight. Building sections, 3D visualization, or explicit note from AE Design confirming line of sight verification is needed. Without this verification, it is unclear whether all transformer-to-meter pairs meet the line of sight requirement.
findings.comment: Direct line of sight from transformers to meters not verified. Provide line of sight analysis or building sections confirming unobstructed visual path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter location(s), or provide documented AE Design approval for exceptions.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads are shown adjacent to paved internal driveways. The 1" = 20' scale plan shows the pads in proximity to driveways, but no specific width dimensions are labeled for the access routes to the transformer pads. Sheet 9 shows driveway details referencing "Construct Type III Driveway See Detail 433S-2", but transformer-specific access route width requirements are not explicitly dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 12-foot horizontal width for truck access paths to transformer pads. While the plans show transformer pads adjacent to driveways, the width of the access path from the drivable surface to the transformer pad is not dimensionally verified. Typical internal site driveways may be 12-20 feet wide overall, but the specific access route to each transformer pad must meet the 12-foot minimum. Without dimensional verification at the transformer pad locations, compliance is unclear.
findings.comment: Horizontal width of truck access paths to transformer pads not dimensionally verified. Provide dimensioned site plan showing minimum 12-foot width access route from drivable surface to each transformer pad, measured at the narrowest point of the access path.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows extensive contour lines and spot elevations across the site, indicating significant grade changes (9+ feet total elevation change across site). However, transformer pad locations are NOT shown on the grading plan. Building Finished Floor Elevations (FFE) are provided but transformer pad elevations are not. Without transformer pad elevations and spot elevations along the access routes, the vertical clearances and access route slopes cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for truck access paths to transformer pads. This clearance must be verified by checking building heights, overhead structures, and any other obstructions above the access route. The grading plan does not show transformer pad locations or their associated vertical clearance zones. Without this information, it is impossible to verify that 16-foot vertical clearance is maintained along all access paths. Any overhead structures, eaves, awnings, or other features crossing above the access routes would need to be checked against this requirement.
findings.comment: Vertical clearance of truck access paths to transformer pads not verified. Provide grading plan or building section details showing transformer pad locations with spot elevations, and verify that minimum 16-foot vertical clearance is maintained along all access routes to transformer pads, including clearances from building eaves, overhangs, and any other overhead structures.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads appear to be within approximately 6 feet of drivable surfaces based on visual scale assessment (1" = 20'). The pads are shown as rectangular symbols in landscaped islands immediately adjacent to paved driveways. However, no specific dimension lines or measurements are labeled on the plans to confirm the exact distance from each pad to the nearest drivable surface. If any transformers are more than 6 feet from a drivable surface, a 20-foot all-weather access route would be required, but no such access routes are explicitly shown or called out on the plans.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformers to be either: (1) within 6 feet of a drivable surface with standard access, or (2) if more than 6 feet away, served by a 20-foot all-weather access route. The plans do not dimensionally verify the distances from each transformer pad to the drivable surface. While visual inspection suggests all pads are close to driveways, without explicit measurements, it cannot be confirmed that all pads meet this requirement or that adequate access routes are provided. The preliminary nature of the electrical plan means precise distances may not be finalized.
findings.comment: Distance from transformer pads to nearest drivable surface not dimensionally verified on plans. Provide dimensioned measurements from each transformer pad to the nearest drivable surface, confirming either that pads are within 6 feet of drivable surface, or alternatively that 20-foot all-weather access routes are provided where pads exceed 6 feet from drivable surfaces.
